issues.reason: The exact EmergencyStopping state is present, but its closed-model lifecycle carrier is the abstract action EmergencyStopSendObstacleDetected rather than the independently required action Emergency Stop. The supplied frozen S4 predicate cannot represent this combined state-level lifecycle carrier as the exact required action contract.
issues.requirement_quote: When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The combined closed-model action might semantically encode both Emergency Stop and the Obstacle Detected emission, but the supplied closure does not provide a typed decomposition proving that equivalence.
issues.title: EmergencyStopping action carrier does not expose the required action

issues.basis: NL3 effect obligation; PlantUML EmergencyStopping annotation; FCSTM EmergencyStopping lifecycle action and transition inventory, which contains no EmergencyStopping transition effect for Obstacle Detected.
issues.expected: EmergencyStopping sends the Obstacle Detected signal.
issues.observed: The closed model has no separately typed EmergencyStopping effect carrier for Obstacle Detected; only combined abstract action EmergencyStopSendObstacleDetected is exposed.
issues.reason: The exact state and source lifecycle effect are identified, but the closed model supplies only a combined abstract lifecycle action and no separately typed effect for sending Obstacle Detected. This is a precise semantic gap at the state-level effect boundary.
issues.requirement_quote: When an obstacle is detected, the system enters the EmergencyStopping state, which includes the actions "Emergency Stop" and sends the "Obstacle Detected" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The combined abstract lifecycle action could encode the signal emission, but no supplied typed fact establishes that it does.
issues.title: EmergencyStopping signal effect lacks a typed carrier

issues.basis: NL5 owner/target hints; exact source child InMotion.Accelerating; inspection transition:line:18 from [*] to UnspecifiedInitial; working contract identifies UnspecifiedInitial as compiler-owned synthetic state.
issues.expected: The InMotion owner-local initial edge enters Accelerating.
issues.observed: The InMotion owner-local initial edge enters state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:17, a compiler-owned synthetic placeholder.
issues.reason: The exact InMotion owner-local initial edge exists, but it enters the compiler-owned UnspecifiedInitial placeholder instead of the required Accelerating child. The separate root edge into DoorsClosing does not satisfy this nested owner-local entry obligation.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The placeholder might be intended as an implementation device that later selects Accelerating, but the supplied FCSTM contains no such selection edge and the source-to-model mapping marks it synthetic.
issues.title: InMotion default entry targets a synthetic placeholder

issues.basis: NL10 exact retention contract; inspection and verification facts provide topology and reachability only, while SMT facts concern unrelated route-token guards.
issues.expected: The system remains in Approaching during the stated nearing-destination interval until readiness to stop or decelerate.
issues.observed: No supplied trace or typed interval/readiness fact evaluates retention of Approaching.
issues.reason: The exact state is bound, but the closure supplies no trace scenario, stimulus, readiness condition, or interval fact that could evaluate the state-retention obligation. The absence of such a trace is an unsupported evaluation boundary, not a claim that the state leaves prematurely.
issues.requirement_quote: The system remains in the Approaching substate while nearing the destination, until it is ready to stop or decelerate.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: A future native trace adapter could materialize the required scenario and determine retention; the current closure does not provide that scenario.
issues.title: Approaching retention cannot be evaluated from supplied facts

issues.basis: NL5 requires InMotion to initially enter Accelerating; source inventory maps InMotion.Accelerating; closed inspection facts show transition:line:18 from the InMotion initial pseudostate to state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:17, while state:Accelerating:line:10 is not reached.
issues.expected: The initial pseudostate owned by InMotion enters Accelerating.
issues.observed: The InMotion initial pseudostate enters UnspecifiedInitial; Accelerating is unreachable from the top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The exact InMotion-owned initial edge exists but targets the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state rather than Accelerating. The required owner-local entry therefore does not enter the specified child.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the Accelerating substate, moving to the Cruising substate once cruising speed is reached, as indicated by the "Reached Cruising/Cruise" signal.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The model does contain an InMotion initial edge, but its exact target is UnspecifiedInitial, so that edge cannot satisfy the required Accelerating target.
issues.title: InMotion Initial Entry Targets the Wrong Child

issues.basis: NL4 defines InMotion's required operating substates; inspection-equivalent and finite verification facts refute reachability for Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching; the closed root reaches InMotion only through UnspecifiedInitial.
issues.expected: The InMotion operating scope must provide root-reachable required operating substates.
issues.observed: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching are all marked unreachable from the top-level initial entry, while only UnspecifiedInitial is reached inside InMotion.
issues.reason: The required operating substates are present in the closed model but none is reachable from the system's top-level initial entry. This is a root-reachability consequence distinct from the malformed InMotion local initial edge.
issues.requirement_quote: Within the InMotion state, the system operates in three substates: Accelerating, Cruising, and Approaching, which represent different phases of the train's motion.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The required child declarations and local transitions exist, but the finite root reachability facts explicitly show that none of the three required operating substates can be reached from the initial entry.
issues.title: Required InMotion Operating States Are Unreachable
